cards.prose: Peter did not work this out for himself, and Yahusha (Jesus) says so. In the same way he thanks the Father that these things are hidden from *the wise and prudent* and shown to *babes*. Who the Son is gets seen only where the Father opens the eyes.
cards.member_phrase: thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) thanks the Father for hiding these things from the wise and giving them to babes, which is how Peter received his answer.

cards.prose: Moses' song names the one who is *the Rock*, and says his way is just and right. A hearer who knew that song would not hear *upon this rock* as a man's name but as the one Peter had just confessed, the Son of the living Elohim (God).
cards.member_phrase: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he
cards.member_sentence: Moses' song calls Elohim (God) himself the Rock, perfect in work and just in all his ways, which is the Rock Peter's confession points to.

cards.prose: David ran to Yahuah (the LORD) as his *rock*, his fortress and his deliverer. When Yahusha (Jesus) says *upon this rock I will build*, he speaks of the same strong place, the one Peter had just named, and not of Peter himself.
cards.member_phrase: my Elohim (God), my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation
cards.member_sentence: David calls Yahuah (the LORD) his rock, fortress and deliverer, the strong place the building of Matthew 16 stands on.

cards.prose: Paul says the Rock that followed Yashar'el (Israel) through the wilderness was Messiah (Christ). So the Rock Moses sang of and the Rock of Caesarea Philippi are one, the one the fathers were given to drink from, now standing in the flesh before Peter.
cards.member_sentence: Paul names the Rock that followed the fathers in the wilderness as Messiah (Christ), the same one Peter confessed.

cards.prose: Peter himself later writes of *a living stone*, refused by men and chosen of Elohim (God). He does not point at himself. He points at the one he came to, which tells us what he understood Yahusha (Jesus) to mean by the rock.
cards.member_sentence: Peter writes of a living stone refused by men and chosen of Elohim (God), pointing away from himself to the one he confessed.

cards.prose: The house is built on the apostles and the prophets, with Yahusha (Jesus) as the corner stone that holds it. Because the prophets are in the foundation too, what Yahusha (Jesus) builds is not a new house begun at Caesarea Philippi but the old one.
cards.member_sentence: The house stands on the apostles and prophets with Yahusha (Jesus) as chief corner stone, so the building is as old as the prophets.

cards.prose: The builders refused a stone that became the head of the corner. Peter has just named that stone, and Yahusha (Jesus) goes on at once to speak of the elders and chief priests and scribes who will cast him off, the builders of this psalm.
cards.member_sentence: The stone the builders refused becomes the head stone of the corner, the rock Peter confessed and the leaders were about to reject.

cards.prose: Hezekiah speaks of the *gates of the grave* as the place where a man is shut in at the end of his days. These are the gates Yahusha (Jesus) means, and he says they will not prevail against what he builds.
cards.member_phrase: I shall go to the gates of the grave: I am deprived of the residue of my years
cards.member_sentence: Hezekiah says he is going to the gates of the grave, the shut place of the dead that Yahusha (Jesus) says will not prevail.

cards.prose: The psalmist cries to Yahuah (the LORD), who *liftest me up from the gates of death*. The gates are real and they hold the dead, but they are not the last word for the one he lifts.
cards.member_phrase: thou that liftest me up from the gates of death
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist is lifted by Yahuah (the LORD) from the gates of death, showing those gates are not where the story stops.

cards.prose: The same words that went to Peter go to all the disciples here, and they come right after the matter of a brother who will not hear and a word that must be settled *in the mouth of two or three witnesses* (Matthew 18:16). The keys are a stewardship of the house, used the way Moses taught a matter to be judged, under the Father and not over him.
cards.member_phrase: Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven
cards.member_sentence: The binding and loosing given to Peter is given to the disciples together, set among witnesses and a brother who will not hear.

cards.prose: Isaiah asks to whom the arm of Yahuah (the LORD) is revealed. Peter had just been shown who the Son is by the Father; now the same arm is shown in suffering, and Peter turns from it. The prophet already knew few would believe that report.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah opens the suffering servant with the question who will believe the report, the very report Peter could not take.

cards.prose: The one who must suffer is the Shepherd, and in Zechariah it is Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts himself who wakes the sword against him. The sheep are scattered when he is smitten, which is the road Yahusha (Jesus) says he must go.
cards.member_phrase: smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) of hosts bids the sword smite the Shepherd, so his death is the appointed road and the sheep scatter.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says he must go to Jerusalem and be killed, and Zechariah names the very place. The one speaking says *look upon me whom they have pierced*, and the house of David and Jerusalem mourn him *as one mourneth for his only son*.
cards.member_phrase: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah has Yahuah (the LORD) speak of a pierced one in Jerusalem, mourned as an only son, the one Yahusha (Jesus) says must die there.

cards.prose: He says it again while they are still in Galilee, and now adds that the Son of Adam will be *betrayed into the hands of men*. The ending is the same, killed and raised the third day, and he does not soften it for them by saying it only once.
cards.member_sentence: A second time Yahusha (Jesus) tells them he will be killed and raised, and now adds that he will be betrayed into the hands of men.

cards.prose: What he first said at Caesarea Philippi is now being walked. Here he is *going up to Jerusalem* with the twelve taken apart, and for the third time he tells them plainly what waits for him there.
cards.member_sentence: The third telling comes on the road up to Jerusalem itself, with the twelve taken apart and told what will be done to him.

cards.prose: On the high mountain the devil offered all the kingdoms and their glory with no cross in the way. Peter's *this shall not be unto thee* offers the same thing again through a friend's mouth, and the answer is the same, *Get thee behind me, Satan* (Matthew 16:23).
cards.member_sentence: The devil showed him all the kingdoms and their glory with no cross, the same offer Peter makes in saying this shall not be.

cards.prose: The tree is the way he is killed, and Paul says he was made a curse for us there. That curse is the judgment the covenant itself laid on those who broke it, the scattering. It is not the commandments, which are what he brings the scattered home to.
cards.member_phrase: Messiah (Christ) hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Messiah (Christ) took the curse of hanging on a tree, the covenant's judgment on the breakers, not the commandments.
cards.flag: Old note read the curse as the exile judgment; kept, and said plainly that the commandments are not the curse.

cards.prose: Sin has no dominion over the one raised with him, because the road home through his death is open. That is grace as the way back to the commandments. Paul asks the next question himself: *shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? Elohim (God) forbid.* (Romans 6:15)
cards.member_sentence: Paul says sin shall not rule those brought through his death, and means the door home, not a release from the commandments.
cards.flag: Kept the old note's point (the way home and the curse still real) and said it without setting grace against the commandments.

cards.prose: He said it first when he sent the twelve out, and it comes back now with Jerusalem and the cross in view. *Take up his cross* is not new to them, but after the passion foretold they can hear where it leads.
cards.member_sentence: The same cost of discipleship was named when he sent out the twelve: whoever will not take his cross and follow is not worthy of him.

cards.prose: Matthew sets it as a trade of one life for another, *lose it* and *find it*. John says which life is given up, the one loved *in this world*, and which is kept, the life that has no end.
cards.member_sentence: John gives the same sentence and names the life let go and the life kept, the one in this world and the life eternal.

cards.prose: In the wilderness the devil offered *the whole world* and the glory of it, and Yahusha (Jesus) refused it. That is why he can ask what a man profits who gains the whole world and loses his own soul.
cards.member_sentence: The devil offered all the kingdoms and their glory and was refused, which is the bargain Yahusha (Jesus) says no man should make.

cards.prose: The same Son of Adam comes with the angels, and Matthew 25 shows where the reward is given. He sits on the throne of his glory and divides the sheep from the goats, so reward according to works is the sorting itself, *he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats* (Matthew 25:32).
cards.member_phrase: then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam comes in his glory with his angels and sits on his throne, where each is rewarded and the sheep are divided from the goats.

cards.prose: The Son of Adam who rewards each by his works is the one who sowed the good seed, *He that soweth the good seed is the Son of Adam* (Matthew 13:37). The reapers of that harvest are the angels who come with him, and the reward is the sorting of wheat and tares.
cards.member_phrase: his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field
cards.member_sentence: The disciples ask the parable of the tares, and the Son of Adam who sows the seed is the one who comes with the reapers.

cards.prose: He had said some standing there would not taste of death first, and six days later he takes three of them up the mountain. What they see there is a foretaste, *his face did shine as the sun* (Matthew 17:2), and the coming in glory itself is still ahead.
cards.member_sentence: Six days later Peter, James and John are taken up the mountain and shown a foretaste of the Son of Adam in his glory.

cards.prose: Peter was one of those standing there, and he writes that they did not follow *cunningly devised fables* but were witnesses of his majesty. He calls it the power and coming of Yahusha (Jesus), so what they saw on the mountain was real and pointed to the coming itself.
cards.member_phrase: but were eyewitnesses of his majesty
cards.member_sentence: Peter, who stood on the mountain, says they were eyewitnesses of his majesty and followed no devised fables.

cards.prose: He gave the scribes and Pharisees these same words earlier, and when the Pharisees and Sadducees ask again for a sign from heaven he gives the same answer. The people who ask for signs are *adulterous*, unfaithful to the covenant, and the one sign is Jonah, who went down into the deep and came up.
cards.member_phrase: there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonah
cards.member_sentence: Earlier Yahusha (Jesus) answered the scribes and Pharisees with the very same words about the one sign of Jonah.

cards.prose: Isaiah is where the word *adulterous* comes from, the faithful city turned harlot, once full of judgment and now full of murderers. Yahusha (Jesus) puts the generation that demands a sign in that line, because Yahuah (the LORD) is the husband and they have left him.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah laments the faithful city turned harlot, the prophets' picture of covenant unfaithfulness that Yahusha (Jesus) calls adulterous.

cards.prose: The men in the boat said it in awe after the wind stopped. Peter says it at Caesarea Philippi with no storm quieted, and the Father had shown it to him. It is the same title, spoken once at a wonder and once at a revealing.
cards.member_sentence: After he walked on the sea the men in the boat worshipped him as the Son of Elohim (God), the first sounding of Peter's confession.

cards.prose: Peter did not reason his way to this. The Father who sent the Son is the one who draws, and Peter's answer is that drawing showing in his mouth. Those drawn are drawn to something, for the Son says he will *raise him up at the last day*.
cards.member_sentence: No one comes to the Son unless the Father draws him, which is what Yahusha (Jesus) says happened to Peter.

cards.prose: Paul had been taught zealously by men and persecuted the assembly. What turned him was no teacher but Elohim (God), who separated him from the womb and was pleased *to reveal his Son in me* (Galatians 1:16), the same Father's revealing Peter received.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Elohim (God) himself separated and called him and revealed his Son in him, as the Father revealed him to Peter.

cards.prose: The gates of hell are the gates of death, and Paul says death is *swallowed up in victory* when the dead are raised incorruptible. That is why those gates will not prevail against what Yahusha (Jesus) builds.
cards.member_phrase: Death is swallowed up in victory
cards.member_sentence: Paul says that when the dead are raised incorruptible, death is swallowed up in victory, which is why the gates cannot prevail.

cards.prose: He had given the Pharisees only the sign of Jonah. Now he tells his own disciples what that sign is: that he must be killed and raised the third day.
cards.member_phrase: there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonah
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) once told the Pharisees they would have only the sign of Jonah, and now he says plainly what it means.

cards.prose: Luke gives the same saying in other words, *cannot be my disciple*. Bearing the cross is not an extra for the very devoted but the plain mark of the one who comes after him.
cards.member_sentence: Luke gives the same saying and says whoever does not bear his cross and come after him cannot be his disciple.

cards.prose: Just before it, John has the grain of wheat that *fall into the ground and die* (John 12:24), and that is the cross the disciple is told to take up. The grain dies and bears much fruit, and the one who gives up his life in this world keeps it unto eternal life.
cards.member_sentence: John sets the cross-bearing sentence beside the grain of wheat that dies and bears fruit, the life lost and kept.

cards.prose: Reward according to works is not strange to the Sermon. There the question is who *doeth the will of my Father*, and the ones who only say *Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord)* are told, *depart from me, ye that work iniquity* (Matthew 7:23). The Son of Adam rewards what a man did.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: The ones who enter the kingdom are those who do the Father's will, not those who only say Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord).

cards.prose: The Son of Adam says nothing new here. David already said that mercy belongs to Yahuah (the LORD) and that he *renderest to every man according to his work*. Mercy and reward by works sit in the same verse.
cards.member_sentence: David says mercy belongs to Yahuah (the LORD) and that he renders to every man according to his work.

cards.prose: Paul says it as plainly as the Son of Adam does, that Elohim (God) *will render to every man according to his deeds*. The man who wrote so much about faith did not make the reward by deeds go away.
cards.member_sentence: Paul states that Elohim (God) will render to every man according to his deeds, the same standard the Son of Adam names.

cards.prose: Matthew says the Son of Adam comes with his angels, and Zechariah names who else comes with him, *all the saints*. They are a people with him and not angels, the righteous raised and the scattered gathered to him, coming at the place Zechariah names.
cards.member_phrase: and Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God) shall come, and all the saints with thee
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah says Yahuah (the LORD) comes and all the saints with him, naming who comes beside the angels.
